intro: Vedic astrology, or Jyotish, is one of the oldest systems of astrology still in practice. A consultation uses your date, time and place of birth to prepare a chart, which then becomes the starting point for a structured conversation about the areas of life you want to think through.
what_is: Jyotish maps the positions of the planets and lunar mansions (nakshatras) at the moment of birth. Practitioners read the chart through houses, signs, planetary periods (dashas) and transits. It is a traditional interpretive framework, not an empirical science, and a good consultation is clear about that.
process: Dr. Anameka prepares your chart in advance, studies the questions you have shared, and reads the chart with those questions in mind. The session focuses on your priorities rather than a general recitation of every placement.

procedure.body: An unhurried session online or in person, with time for your follow-up questions.

faqs.a: No responsible practitioner can promise that. Consultations are offered as guidance and reflection, and the decisions remain yours.

title: Graphology
short_description: Handwriting analysis that looks at how you write as a starting point for self-reflection.
intro: Graphology is the study of handwriting: its size, slant, pressure, spacing, margins and letter forms. A consultation uses these features as prompts for a conversation about personal tendencies and patterns.
what_is: Graphologists observe recurring features of handwriting and interpret them within a structured framework. Its scientific validity as a personality measure is debated, and it should not be used as the sole basis for decisions such as hiring.

No birth details required

It cannot diagnose health or mental health conditions
Should not be used as the sole basis for employment or legal decisions

faqs.q: How should I prepare a handwriting sample?
faqs.a: Write naturally on unruled paper about half a page to a page, using your normal pen and pace, and sign at the end. Avoid copying text or writing unusually neatly.

faqs.a: No. Graphology is not a medical or diagnostic tool, and any health concern should be taken to a qualified doctor.
